scene beginningoftheend5
: There’s nothing I can say that will make it any less painful.
: Send us back...
: I can’t.
scene beginningoftheend6
: Why?! You’re the one who brought us there!
: Where’s your door?! I want to go back! I want to see my daughter!
: That Himawari is gone now...
: You will have to make do with this one.
: What do you mean “gone?!” What did you do?! Where did she go?!
: She was never anywhere to begin with.
: Neither of you were.
: And if I didn’t get you out of there, I would have never seen you again.
: I apologize for being so selfish. And for all the pain that I have caused you.
: I am a terrible, horrible waste of a girl.
: You were never supposed to see that.
: See what?! A happy ending?! So you had to bring us back here?!
: Would it have been too much to just let us have that?! Have we done something to deserve this punishment?!
: Ayane...I’m sure it isn’t like that.
scene beginningoftheend7
: How can you say that?! We just watched her delete our daughter and our life in less than ten seconds and now we’re right back where we started!
: That is our daughter. She’s right there.
: Right, Himawari? It’s still you, isn’t it?
scene beginningoftheend8
: I’m not allowed to answer that question.
: But...
: Yes.
: I’m still me...
: But I’ve robbed you of the only bit of happiness that you have ever had.
: And for that, I don’t deserve to call myself your daughter. Nor do I deserve to appear before you at all.
scene beginningoftheend9
: But I’m running out of options...and you’re running out of time. So I don’t know what to do anymore! I keep making mistakes!
scene beginningoftheend10
: How are we running out of time here and not the other way around?...
: This life was inescapable until you showed up. Then you finally got us out and now you’re telling us it’s all going to come to an end?
: Then why not let it end where we were happy? As a family?
: I don’t want my final days to be here...
: I want to see Aomori again...
: Himawari, when you say we’re running out of time-
scene beginningoftheend11
: I mean that this place should not exist either.
: And that soon, someone like me is going to come and cleanse it.
: There will be no more “resets” like you call them. No more chances to start over. And the two of you will go back to where you’re meant to be.
: Which is...where?
: That’s what I’m trying to figure out.
: Because I can help...but not if I don’t know where to take you. And just shoving you into another world puts everyone there in jeopardy if someone finds out.
: Is that...why we had to leave? We were...putting Hima-chan in jeopardy?
scene beginningoftheend12
: Not...exactly.
: What was that then? Where were we? Because you made it sound like it was just going to be dark when we walked through that door and not the literal perfect world we found ourselves in.
scene beginningoftheend13
: Heh...it was perfect, wasn’t it?
: Spending every day together...hanging out on the couch and watching TV...going to arcades and restaurants all the time...eating Mom’s breakfast every morning...
: I’d give anything to exist there.
scene beginningoftheend14
: That’s why I made it.
: What?...
: That’s my world.
: My wish.
: A place outside of everything — where the three of us can be happy.
: A place that feels like it moves, where the seasons change and people grow. But it’s just like this one at the end of the day.
: A lie based on a desire. An endless yearning for a positive outcome, granted physical form for no reason other than to make one person happy. But that sort of thing always comes with a caveat.
scene beginningoftheend15
: You thought it when you woke up there, right? That it all seemed too good to be true?
: Yeah...and I feel pretty vindicated in thinking that right now. What do you mean you made it, though? You just...wished it and it happened?
: That’s the short explanation, yeah. The longer one gets deep into the machinations of various gods in different tiers of godliness who treat this place more like a sandbox than an actual universe.
: Are you saying you’re...a god?
scene beginningoftheend16
: Me? No. Of course not.
: But that doesn’t mean I don’t work with them.
scene beginningoftheend17
: You...
: Sorry. You work with gods?
: Mhm! Not directly, but under the same parent company.
: I’m sort of a...celestial custodian or something along those lines. I clean up worlds that...well, require cleaning.
: But after a certain point, some worlds just aren’t worth cleaning anymore.
: Think of it like a...server for a game that nobody wants to play or something. That just gets shut down after a while because it’s effectively dead.
: And those worlds are the result of...wishes?
: There’s a real world too, of course. At least on a technical level.
: But the vast majority of worlds are born from wishes, yes. The sad part is that, most of the time, the people who wish for them don’t even know it.
: So they live and die in the world where they made a wish while a second version of them reaps the benefits of their desires. It’s all super complex and weird. Orientation for the job is rough.
: If there’s a real world, though...isn’t that where we’re from?...Can’t we all go there together and just...start over?...
: You’d think. But normal people aren’t allowed there. It’s reserved for the gods. Not even us custodians are allowed to see it.
: But, from what I hear, we’d probably go blind if we could. So I guess it’s sort of good that they don’t let us in.
: So...you’re saying...
: This world is a wish too?
scene black
: That’s right...
: But here’s where things start to get really messy.
scene beginningoftheend18
: Because it’s not just worlds that are born from wishes.
: Sometimes, people are too. Or things. Hell, even Kit-Kat flavors could be zapped into reality if someone wishes for them hard enough.
: But we all only get one. And since most of us use them without even knowing, the vast majority wind up as different worlds or people. Things that humans deeply desire.
: Now, Father — let’s say I’m the result of a wish. Which I’m not, just to clarify. I’m your real, blood-related future daughter. Your genes swim through me like tilapia in the Nile.
: But let’s say I was. From your standpoint as a regular law-unabiding gentleman, if I wished deeply enough for something as a wish myself, what do you think would happen?
: Probably...nothing? There wouldn’t be enough “custodians” to clean anything up if the universe could snowball like that.
scene beginningoftheend19
: Exactly. And why we’re all secretly hoping in the office that more people start wishing for Kit-Kats.
scene beginningoftheend20
: But, let’s say it did work.
: That somehow, there was a wish that wished so strongly, it defied the logic of this world and broke the very laws that gave it life in the first place.
: What then?
: I don’t know, Himawari...
: Do you think that the ones in control of this universe would allow something like that to exist? Something that, at least on paper, is more powerful than they are?
: Probably...not? Most of the gods I’ve met haven’t exactly seemed rational or understanding. But it’s possible they’d keep an eye on it to-
: That.
: That’s exactly it.
: They’d keep an eye on it. Make sure nothing gets out of hand.
: But even their time isn’t infinite. And once it’s no longer reasonable or even entertaining to do so, there’d be no reason to keep it. Or even give it room to grow.
: Now, based on everything I just said-
: What kind of world do you think this is?
: I...get what you’re saying. But who-
: You know exactly who. But in the event that I really am just infinitely smarter than you, allow me to spell it out.
: Maya Makinami does not exist.
: This is a world of her creation. One that breaks so many rules that I can’t even trace where it comes from.
scene beginningoftheend21
: And it’s because of that that I’m having so much trouble helping you and Mom.
: If I only knew where you were before here, I’m sure I could get you out.
: I might lose my job in the process, sure. But that’s obviously a risk I’m willing to take if it means saving-
: That’s enough.
scene beginningoftheend22
: What do you mean that’s enough? I’m breaking like a thousand laws by just telling you this. If anyone finds out I did, I’m-
: I understand.
scene beginningoftheend23
: You...
: You do?
: Not perfectly. But I know you wouldn’t lie to me. And I don’t want what little time I have left with you before you leave again to be filled with corporate, religious psychobabble.
scene beginningoftheend24
: You do have to leave again, right?
: They’re catching on...
: They know how much time I spend here now.
: I’m not supposed to come at all anymore. I can’t just...leave you guys alone, though. I worry too much and-
: You never have to explain yourself to me, Himawari. You could lead me off a cliff for all I care.
: I’ll follow you anywhere. Whether it be this world or-
scene beginningoftheend25
: Aomori?...
: Or Aomori...
: You’d take me there again?...
: Even after what I did?...
: It’s your wish, isn’t it?
scene beginningoftheend26
: It’s...the reason I do this...
scene beginningoftheend27
: I, uhh...
: I don’t think Mom is on the same page right now, though...
scene black
: Ayane...what are you doing?
scene beginningoftheend28
: She’s still here. We still have time with her.
: Not...much, though. I, uhh...
: I have cleaning duty again. No one’s touched this place since I made you guys walk through Despacito.
: I can’t do it...
: It hurts too much...
: I know...
: But what I know even more is how much you’ll regret letting this chance slip through your fingers.
: Everything slipped through my fingers...
: It was all right there...I can still see it...
: I didn’t even turn the stove off...and Hima-chan has clothes in the dryer...
scene beginningoftheend29
: I had work today...
: I don’t know what happens if I don’t show up...
: Ayane...
: What’s gonna happen if she comes back home and no one’s there to greet her?...
: I, uhh...
: I’m gonna...head over to the beach and...start cleaning up now...
: But I should have a little time left over to come back and...
scene black
: Wait...
My feet move on their own.
And, for once, I'm thankful for that.
scene beginningoftheend30
: I’m coming with you.
: You’re...
: You’re what?
: Coming with you. Pay more attention.
: I was, just...
: Because I’ll regret it if I don’t. And I want to see my daughter at work.
: But...
: What about Mom? You’re just...going to leave her here?
: She’ll come to her senses soon. And if for some reason she doesn’t, we can just turn this into another date.
scene beginningoftheend31
: And get totally smashed in the purikura booths?...
: That’s how we do it.
: You know my job isn’t exactly...pretty, right? Like, I’m...going to be reformatting all of your...uhh...
: Friends is just...what I’ll call them.
: I just watched my daughter get turned into TV static. I think I can handle a little reformatting.
scene beginningoftheend32
: Hahah! Yeah...probably a walk in the park after that.
scene beginningoftheend33
: Are you ready to go now then? I can introduce you to one of my friends.
: You have friends? Since when? It better not be a boy.
: It’s a girl. Shi-chan. She’s off limits, though. So don’t even think about it.
: She...works for the same, uhh...company then?
scene beginningoftheend34
: She’s my senpai and she’s super cool! I got to shadow her for the first month and she’s, like...totally dead inside.
: Oh. Cool.
scene black
: You know, I have a friend like that too. She’s-
: Wakana Watabe! I know! Want me to transform into her? Look!
: How the-
: Oh, right. You wouldn’t remember I can do that. Uhh...surprise! Oh, I can also basically watch your entire life in real time from an app on my phone. Wanna see?
: You can do what?
: Yeah. You’re a real scumbag like 99%% of the time, Dad. I had to turn parental controls on just so I wouldn’t accidentally see you getting it on with one of your students again.
: I’m going to need you to delete that app from your phone.
: Nooo, I need it for work! And for spying. Anyway, ready to learn about another one of my cool custodial powers?
: You’re not the one that’s been causing my blackouts, are you? Is there a button in your app for that?
: God, I wish. That’d be so funny. This power is way more convenient, though. Want to say goodbye to Mom?
: Ayane, last chance. Are you sure you don’t want to-
: Just go...
: I can’t do it...
: Hah...
: In that case — away! To a more depressing daddy-daughter date! Take my hand.
: Like this? What are we-
$ undeservedfuture10 = True
jump undeservedfuture11
